samples.summary: Narrowed ALLOWED_URI_REGEXP strips almost every SVG geometry/presentation attribute, so real diagrams render empty
samples.evidence: `ALLOWED_URI_REGEXP: /^(?:#|https?:\/\/|mailto:)/i` in PURIFY_CONFIG. DOMPurify's `_isValidAttribute` applies `IS_ALLOWED_URI` to the value of EVERY allowed attribute that is not in `DEFAULT_URI_SAFE_ATTRIBUTES` (`alt,class,for,id,label,name,pattern,placeholder,role,summary,title,value,style,xmlns`) and not `data-*`/`aria-*`; if the value matches neither the URI regexp nor the `data:`/ALLOW_UNKNOWN_PROTOCOLS fallbacks, the branch `else if (value) return false` drops the attribute. That is precisely why DOMPurify's DEFAULT regexp contains the permissive `[^a-z]|[a-z+.\-]+(?:[^a-z+.\-:]|$)` alternatives — to let non-URI values through. Replacing it with `^(?:#|https?://|mailto:)` therefore removes `d="M0,0 L4,2"`, `transform="translate(8,8)"`, `viewBox="0 0 100 100"`, `width/height/x/y`, `stroke-width="2"`, `fill="none"`, `text-anchor`, `points`, `marker-end="url(#id)"` (value starts with `u`, not `#`) etc. from mermaid's output, leaving a structurally-present but unrenderable SVG. No test catches this: every attribute in the fixtures at packages/notes/src/view/preview.test.ts:357-386 is either `data-*` (`data-text`) or URI-safe (`id`, `class`, `style`, `href="#section"`), and real mermaid cannot run under jsdom, so the suite is green while the shipped feature paints blank diagrams.

samples.summary: `xlink:href` is not in the enabled DOMPurify profiles, so the `<use>` tag added by ADD_TAGS loses its reference
samples.evidence: `USE_PROFILES: { svg: true, svgFilters: true, html: true }` resets ALLOWED_ATTR to the union of those three profiles. `xlink:href` lives in DOMPurify's separate `xml` attribute profile, which is not enabled, so a `<use xlink:href="#arrow"/>` keeps the element and loses the only attribute that makes it mean anything — markers/icons emitted with the xlink form silently disappear. The new test at packages/notes/src/view/preview.test.ts ("keeps the in-document references a real diagram is built from") asserts only `block.querySelector('use')` is truthy, never that the reference survived, so the gap is invisible to CI.

samples.summary: CSS_EXTERNAL_RE can false-positive on legitimate mermaid `<style>` output and then drops the diagram's entire stylesheet
samples.evidence: `isSafeCss()` failure removes the whole `<style>` element (mermaid.ts:286). The pattern flags any `src(`/`image(`/`url(` not followed by `#`, so a mermaid stylesheet that contains a `@font-face { src: url(...) }` (e.g. the katex CSS mermaid injects for math labels, or a font-embedding theme) loses ALL of the diagram's styling — the diagram renders as unstyled black-on-white shapes with no diagnostic. A rule that dropped just the offending declaration, or that scoped the check to off-page URLs only, would not have this cliff.

samples.summary: `flush()` (one `setTimeout(0)`) may not cover the newly added real `import('dompurify')`, making the mermaid render assertions timing-dependent
samples.evidence: renderPass now awaits `Promise.all([load(), loadPurifier()])` (mermaid.ts:380) and `loadPurifier()` performs a REAL dynamic import even when the engine is stubbed; `resetMermaidStateForTests()` nulls `purifier` before every case so the promise is recreated each time. The tests wait exactly one macrotask (`new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 0))`), which is not guaranteed to cover the first module resolution (transform + fs read) in vitest — the assertions on rendered SVG can flake on a cold module graph or slow CI runner.

samples.summary: An unterminated `%%{` anywhere in a fence swallows the rest of the diagram source
samples.evidence: DIRECTIVE_RE ends in `(?:}%{2})?` with the body alternative `((?:(?!}%{2}).|\r?\n)*)`, so a stray `%%{` — including one inside a node label, e.g. `A["%%{"] --> B` — consumes everything to the end of the fence. The user then sees a generic "Diagram error" for text that looks valid. Mermaid reads the same span, so behaviour is consistent, but the failure mode is opaque and untested.

verdict.reason: The narrowed ALLOWED_URI_REGEXP (^(?:#|https?://|mailto:) with /i) is present verbatim at packages/notes/src/view/mermaid.ts:229, inside PURIFY_CONFIG, with no ADD_URI_SAFE_ATTR and no uponSanitizeAttribute hook anywhere in the repo (grep for addHook/ADD_URI_SAFE_ATTR returns only doc-comment hits). With dompurify ^3.4.12 (packages/notes/package.json:63), _isValidAttribute applies IS_ALLOWED_URI to the value of every allowed attribute that is not data-*/aria-* and not in DEFAULT_URI_SAFE_ATTRIBUTES, falling through to `else if (value) return false`; the default regexp's permissive non-URI alternatives are exactly what normally lets values like d, fill, transform, width/height, viewBox, points, stroke-width, text-anchor and marker-end="url(#id)" through. Replacing them strips those attributes. The path is reachable on every diagram: mermaid.ts:419 sanitizes engine output and apply() at mermaid.ts:445 inserts the fragment via replaceChildren, so shipped diagrams would render structurally present but blank — a core-flow break. No guard elsewhere mitigates it.

verdict.reason: The finding's premise does not hold. In DOMPurify's `_parseConfig`, the `USE_PROFILES` branches for `svg`, `svgFilters` and `mathMl` each add the profile attribute set AND the separate `xml` attribute set (`['xlink:href','xml:id','xlink:title','xml:space','xmlns:xlink']`); only an html-only profile omits `xml`. Because `PURIFY_CONFIG` enables `svg: true` and `svgFilters: true` (mermaid.ts:210), `xlink:href` is present in the resulting `ALLOWED_ATTR`, so `<use xlink:href="#arrow"/>` keeps its reference; the value `#arrow` also passes the narrowed `ALLOWED_URI_REGEXP` at mermaid.ts:229 (and the SVG2 plain `href` form is covered by the enabled html attribute set). No downstream step strips attributes: sanitizeSvg (mermaid.ts:283-292) only removes unsafe `<style>` elements and `style` attributes. The described misconfiguration ("xml profile not enabled, so xlink:href is dropped") is therefore not present in this code. The weak assertion at preview.test.ts:414 is a test-strength observation, not a correctness defect in my lane, and there is no actual attribute loss for it to hide.
